andhraPradesh.headline: Andhra Pradesh and PanIIT sign declaration for Amaravati deep-tech council and ₹500-crore venture fund
facts: The Government of Andhra Pradesh and PanIIT Alumni India signed the Amaravati PanIIT Declaration at the PanIIT Andhra Pradesh Summit in Vijayawada.
The declaration provides for a permanent PanIIT Amaravati Council to connect IITs, universities, industry and startups.
A ₹500-crore PanIIT Amaravati DeepTech Venture Fund was announced for deep-tech startups and innovation; its announcement does not establish that the fund is already operational.
Plans include 10 industry chairs at AP institutions and a proposed network of 100 IIT mentors for startups.
The declaration also envisages connecting 10 AP universities to the PanIIT ecosystem and incubating at least 50 startups in the state by 2030.
andhraPradesh.summary: At the summit on 3 October, Andhra Pradesh and PanIIT Alumni India signed a declaration setting out institutional and startup-ecosystem initiatives. The council, venture fund and mentorship network are planned initiatives; the source does not establish that they are already operational.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Innovation ecosystems, technology transfer, startup financing and public–private collaboration in state development.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: Remember the PanIIT Amaravati Council, proposed ₹500-crore DeepTech Venture Fund, 10 industry chairs and proposed 100-mentor network.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Assess how alumni–government partnerships, university–industry linkages and patient capital can strengthen regional innovation while requiring transparent governance and measurable outcomes.
andhraPradesh.apLink: Directly concerns Andhra Pradesh; the proposed council is to be based in Amaravati and the initiatives target AP universities and startups.

andhraPradesh.headline: Foundation stone laid for Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub and Indian School of Agriculture at Madanapalle
facts: The foundation stone for the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub and the Indian School of Agriculture was laid at Madanapalle in Annamayya district on 2 October 2026.
The hub is planned across 10 districts and is intended to develop horticulture, including mango, banana, tomato and pomegranate.
The project has an estimated overall investment of about ₹1 lakh crore and is planned for implementation in three phases.
The Indian School of Agriculture is intended to support farmer training, modern agricultural methods and research.
The foundation ceremony marks a project milestone; it does not mean the hub or school is operational.
andhraPradesh.summary: Previous: the Global Horticulture Hub and Indian School of Agriculture had been announced for the Madanapalle region. Today: foundation stones were laid on 2 October, advancing the proposals to the foundation stage. The hub remains a multi-phase project, not an operational facility.

andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The hub’s foundation was laid at Madanapalle, Annamayya district; it is planned across 10 districts with an estimated investment of about ₹1 lakh crore.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Examine whether horticulture-led diversification can improve farm incomes and climate resilience in drought-prone Rayalaseema, alongside the need for reliable irrigation, markets, storage and risk management.

andhraPradesh.headline: Boiler explosion at Sri City industrial unit kills four workers and critically injures one
facts: A boiler exploded at a private industrial unit in Sri City, Satyavedu mandal, Andhra Pradesh, on 3 October 2026.
Akashvani reported four worker deaths and one critically injured worker receiving treatment in an intensive-care unit.
Sri City is a Special Economic Zone in Andhra Pradesh; the reported incident occurred inside a factory.
The Chief Minister directed officials to provide assistance to affected families and attend to the injured.
The available report did not establish the cause of the explosion or report the outcome of any investigation.
andhraPradesh.summary: A boiler explosion at an industrial unit in Sri City caused worker fatalities and serious injury on 3 October. The incident raises issues of industrial safety, emergency response and enforcement, but the cause had not been established in the cited report.
andhraPradesh.staticLink: Industrial disaster preparedness, occupational safety and the state’s regulatory and emergency-response responsibilities.
andhraPradesh.prelimsTakeaway: The reported incident occurred at Sri City in Satyavedu mandal; distinguish the reported casualty count from later or unverified figures.
andhraPradesh.mainsAngle: Discuss how risk-based inspections, boiler maintenance, worker training, emergency plans and transparent investigations can reduce industrial-accident risks in manufacturing zones.

national.headline: Asian Games: India retains men’s hockey gold; Aman Sehrawat wins wrestling gold
facts: India defeated Malaysia 5–1 in the men’s hockey final at the 2026 Asian Games, retaining the title.
The hockey victory was India’s fifth men’s Asian Games gold in the event.
The result secured India direct qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics men’s hockey tournament.
Aman Sehrawat won gold in men’s 57 kg freestyle wrestling, India’s first Asian Games gold in that event.
For the first time, India’s men’s and women’s hockey teams both won gold at the same Asian Games.
national.summary: Previous: India’s Asian Games medal campaign had been covered on 2026-09-27. Today: India added notable final results, including a retained men’s hockey title and Aman Sehrawat’s historic wrestling gold.
national.staticLink: Asian Games; sports as soft power; Olympic qualification
national.prelimsTakeaway: India beat Malaysia 5–1 in the men’s hockey final; Aman Sehrawat won the men’s 57 kg freestyle gold.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how sustained investment in sports ecosystems can strengthen international representation and create pathways from continental success to Olympic qualification.

national.headline: India demonstrates a 5.56-km free-space quantum key distribution link
facts: MeitY reported on 3 October that QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar demonstrated a 5.56-km free-space Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) link.
The field trial between BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar took place on the night of 27–28 September 2026.
The trial reported a quantum bit error rate below 5% and secure-key generation of 230–260 bits per second.
The generated keys were integrated with BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach post-quantum cryptography platform to test end-to-end encryption and decryption.
The demonstration combined QKD hardware over free-space optical channels with post-quantum cryptography software.
national.summary: A MeitY release published on 3 October reported the successful field demonstration, conducted in Gujarat on 27–28 September. The release described the system as India’s first free-space QKD link and presented it as a step toward quantum-resilient communications.
national.prelimsTakeaway: QKD uses quantum principles to establish secure cryptographic keys; this demonstration linked BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar over 5.56 km.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the role of indigenous quantum technologies in securing critical communications, alongside the challenges of scaling, reliability and deployment.

sources.title: India’s First 5.56 km Free-Space Quantum Key Distribution Link Demonstrated
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Electronics & IT

- **Demonstrators:** **QNu Labs**, **BISAG-N** and **IIT Gandhinagar**
- **Link:** **5.56-km** free-space **Quantum Key Distribution (QKD)** link between **BISAG-N** and **IIT Gandhinagar**
# 2. Trial and performance
- **Field-trial dates:** Night of **27–28 September 2026**; conducted in **Gujarat**

- **Integration:** Generated keys integrated with **BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach** post-quantum cryptography platform to test end-to-end encryption and decryption
- **Technology combination:** QKD hardware over free-space optical channels with post-quantum cryptography software

- **Andhra Pradesh link:** No direct AP-specific link established

national.headline: Education Ministry approves five Centres of Excellence for classical-language studies
facts: The Department of Higher Education approved five Centres of Excellence for Classical Assamese, Bengali, Marathi, Pali and Prakrit.
The centres are to be established at Tezpur University, Visva-Bharati University, Deccan College, Central University of Odisha and Central University of Gujarat, respectively.
Their stated focus includes advanced research, preservation, digitisation and wider dissemination of linguistic and literary heritage.
The five centres are located across Assam, West Bengal, Maharashtra, Odisha and Gujarat.
national.summary: The Ministry of Education announced approval of five language-specific Centres of Excellence on 3 October. The proposed centres are intended to strengthen research and preservation of classical-language literature and resources.

national.headline: Great Indian Bustard rewilding process initiated at Desert National Park
facts: On 3 October, Union Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav and Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma participated in initiating the process to release two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards into the wild.
The planned release was to take place the following day at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer; it had not yet occurred as of the 3 October announcement.
The birds were being moved from a soft-release facility as part of the species’ recovery programme.
The project involves the Union environment ministry, Rajasthan Forest Department and scientific conservation work, including the Wildlife Institute of India.
The announcement also noted habitat-restoration efforts and a rewilding aviary at the conservation landscape.
national.summary: On 3 October, officials initiated preparations for a planned release of two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards at Desert National Park. The release was scheduled for 4 October, so the 3 October development was the start of the process, not a completed release.
national.staticLink: In-situ and ex-situ conservation; endangered species recovery; protected areas
national.prelimsTakeaway: The Great Indian Bustard is critically endangered; the planned rewilding site is Desert National Park in Rajasthan.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss how conservation breeding, habitat protection and carefully monitored reintroduction can complement each other in species recovery.

national.headline: Indian Navy ships conclude participation in ASEAN–India Maritime Exercise 2026
facts: INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish concluded India’s participation in the ASEAN–India Maritime Exercise (AIME 2026) on 3 October.
The exercise was conducted in the Philippines under the theme “Anchored in Trust, United at Sea”.
It included harbour and sea phases, with professional exchanges and operational coordination activities.
At sea, the ships participated in humanitarian assistance and disaster relief, visit-board-search-seizure and underway-replenishment drills.
The Indian Navy said the engagement supported interoperability and aligned with India’s Act East Policy and MAHASAGAR vision.
national.summary: The Indian Navy’s two participating ships concluded AIME 2026 in the Philippines on 3 October. The exercise included maritime coordination and operational drills with participating forces.

national.headline: Jal Arpan observed in over 1,850 Gram Panchayats under Jal Jeevan Mission 2.0
facts: Jal Arpan was observed in more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats and villages during Gandhi Jayanti special Gram Sabhas on 2 October.
The observance involved formal handover of completed rural water-supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and Village Water and Sanitation Committees for operation and maintenance.
The Jal Arpan module generated and issued 346 Har Ghar Jal certificates in regional languages.
The ministry reported that 2,691 water-supply assets, including about 700 sources, were geotagged on the same occasion.
The Ministry of Jal Shakti published these nationwide figures on 3 October.
national.summary: The Ministry of Jal Shakti reported on 3 October that Jal Arpan had been observed in more than 1,850 Gram Panchayats during the previous day’s special Gram Sabhas. The reported activities included local handover of completed schemes, regional-language certificates and geotagging of water assets.

national.prelimsTakeaway: Jal Arpan supports formal handover and community-led operation and maintenance of completed rural water schemes.
national.mainsAngle: Assess how local ownership, transparent asset records and community monitoring can improve the sustainability of rural drinking-water infrastructure.

international.headline: Indian parliamentary delegation departs for 153rd IPU Assembly in Tanzania
facts: The Inter-Parliamentary Union (IPU) is a global organisation of national parliaments headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.
The 153rd IPU Assembly was scheduled for 5–9 October 2026 in Arusha, Tanzania, hosted by Tanzania’s National Assembly.
Its theme was “Enhancing good governance and empowering communities through inclusivity, trust and opportunities for all.”
India’s delegation, led by Rajya Sabha Deputy Chairman Harivansh, departed on 3 October.
The announced agenda included democracy, human rights, peace and security, sustainable development, AI, maritime security and climate change.
international.summary: India’s parliamentary delegation departed for the 153rd IPU Assembly, scheduled in Arusha from 5 to 9 October. Its participation provides a forum for parliamentary diplomacy and Indian perspectives on governance and other global issues; the Assembly had not yet taken place on the development date.

international.headline: Crude-oil tanker reports projectile strike off Oman
facts: On 3 October, a crude-oil tanker’s master reported that an unknown projectile struck the vessel about 4 nautical miles east of Oman.
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) reported that all crew members were safe.
No environmental impact had been reported at the time of the report.
The projectile’s origin was not identified in the report; the incident was reported as under investigation.
international.summary: UKMTO reported a projectile strike on a crude-oil tanker east of Oman, with the crew safe and no environmental impact reported. The incident highlights maritime-security risks in the Gulf of Oman, an important sea-lane region; no perpetrator was identified in the cited report.

international.mainsAngle: Discuss the importance of maritime-domain awareness and cooperative protection of commercial shipping for energy and trade security.

international.headline: WHO seeks information from Russia under International Health Regulations after reported lab-worker death
facts: WHO later reported that it contacted Russian health authorities on 3 October to verify media reports about an Irkutsk laboratory worker’s death following severe pneumonia.
Media reports had raised suspicion of pneumonic plague, but the cause of death was not confirmed on the development date.
WHO sought information under Articles 9 and 10 of the International Health Regulations (2005) and requested details relevant to assessment under Article 6.
The WHO report published on 10 October said Russian authorities reported no detected high-threat pathogens among contacts and no evidence of ongoing transmission; the cause remained undetermined.
international.summary: WHO’s subsequent account records that it first contacted Russian authorities on 3 October to verify reports about a laboratory worker’s death and assess potential cross-border public-health implications. Plague was suspected in media reports, not established as the diagnosis; WHO’s later update reported no evidence of ongoing transmission while noting that the cause remained undetermined.
international.staticLink: International Health Regulations; global disease surveillance; laboratory biosafety and biosecurity
international.prelimsTakeaway: IHR Articles 6, 9 and 10 concern notification, information-sharing and WHO verification of events that may have international public-health implications.
international.mainsAngle: Explain how transparent, timely cooperation under the IHR helps manage uncertain health events while avoiding premature conclusions and unnecessary travel restrictions.

- **Instrument:** **International Health Regulations (IHR), 2005**

international.headline: Greece transfers Tsar Samuil’s remains to Bulgaria after bilateral agreement
facts: Bulgaria’s Foreign Ministry reported that the mortal remains of medieval ruler Tsar Samuil were welcomed in Sofia on 3 October.

mcqs.question: Which of the following correctly describes the 153rd IPU Assembly, as stated in the item?
options: It was scheduled for 5–9 October 2026 in Arusha, Tanzania, with the theme of inclusive, trusted and opportunity-enhancing governance.
It was held in Geneva, Switzerland, from 3–7 October 2026, with a theme on maritime security.
It was scheduled for 5–9 October 2026 in Vijayawada, India, with a theme on parliamentary technology.
It was hosted by India’s Parliament in New Delhi from 2–6 October 2026.
mcqs.explanation: The Assembly was scheduled for 5–9 October in Arusha and hosted by Tanzania’s National Assembly. Its theme concerned good governance and empowering communities through inclusivity, trust and opportunities.

mcqs.question: Which set of entities participated in the reported 5.56-km free-space QKD demonstration?
options: QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar
ISRO, RBI and Tezpur University
MeitY, the Indian Navy and the Wildlife Institute of India
PanIIT Alumni India, BISAG-N and the Ministry of Jal Shakti
mcqs.explanation: MeitY reported that QNu Labs, BISAG-N and IIT Gandhinagar demonstrated the link. The trial also integrated generated keys with BISAG-N’s Vedic Kavach platform.

mcqs.question: Which pairing of classical language and institution was included among the five approved Centres of Excellence?
options: Classical Assamese — Tezpur University
Classical Bengali — Deccan College
Classical Marathi — Central University of Gujarat
Classical Pali — Visva-Bharati University
mcqs.explanation: The approved pairings included Classical Assamese at Tezpur University, Bengali at Visva-Bharati University, Marathi at Deccan College, Pali at Central University of Odisha and Prakrit at Central University of Gujarat.

mcqs.question: As of the 3 October announcement, what was the status of the planned release of two captive-bred Great Indian Bustards?
options: The release had been completed at Desert National Park.
The release was planned for the following day at Desert National Park.
The birds had been released at a national park in Andhra Pradesh.
The release had been cancelled after the birds reached the soft-release facility.
mcqs.explanation: The item said the process had been initiated and the planned release at Desert National Park, Jaisalmer, was to take place the following day; it had not yet occurred on 3 October.

mcqs.question: What was the purpose of Jal Arpan as observed during the Gandhi Jayanti special Gram Sabhas?
options: To transfer completed rural water-supply schemes to Gram Panchayats and Village Water and Sanitation Committees for operation and maintenance
To transfer all rural water assets to the Indian Navy for emergency management
To certify newly constructed urban housing for municipal operation
To establish a new national water-quality regulator
mcqs.explanation: Jal Arpan involved the formal handover of completed rural water-supply schemes to local bodies and committees for operation and maintenance.

mcqs.question: Which statement about the proposed PanIIT Amaravati DeepTech Venture Fund is supported by the item?
options: It was announced at ₹500 crore, but the announcement did not establish that the fund was already operational.
It had already disbursed ₹500 crore to operating startups.
It was approved as a ₹500-crore central government scheme for all Indian states.
It was established solely to fund the Rayalaseema horticulture hub.
mcqs.explanation: The declaration announced a ₹500-crore fund for deep-tech startups and innovation; the item explicitly distinguishes the announcement from the fund being operational.

mcqs.question: Which statement best describes the Rayalaseema Global Horticulture Hub milestone reported on 2 October 2026?
options: Its foundation stone was laid at Madanapalle; the hub was planned across 10 districts and was not yet operational.
The hub was completed and began operating across 10 districts.
Its foundation stone was laid in Sri City for a single-district horticulture project.
The project was a completed farmer-training school with no proposed horticulture component.
mcqs.explanation: The foundation stone was laid at Madanapalle in Annamayya district. The project was planned across 10 districts and in three phases; the ceremony did not mean the hub or school was operational.

mcqs.question: Which pair of Indian Navy ships concluded India’s participation in AIME 2026?
options: INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish
INS Sahyadri and INS Vikramaditya
INS Kulish and INS Arihant
INS Vikramaditya and INS Arihant
mcqs.explanation: INS Sahyadri and INS Kulish concluded India’s participation in the exercise in the Philippines, which included harbour and sea phases.
